cards.title: A shorter way
cards.body: `const double = n => n * 2;` does the same as a `function` that returns `n * 2`.

hi.title: Chhota tareeka
hi.body: `const double = n => n * 2;` wahi karta hai jo `n * 2` return karne wala `function` karta hai.

cards.title: More parameters
cards.body: With two or more parameters, wrap them in brackets: `(a, b) => a + b`.
cards.code:
const add = (a, b) => a + b;
console.log(add(2, 3));

hi.title: Zyada parameters
hi.body: Do ya zyada parameters hon toh unhe brackets mein rakho: `(a, b) => a + b`.

cards.title: Returning true or false
cards.body: A comparison gives `true` or `false`, so a function can return one directly.

hi.title: true ya false return karna
hi.body: Comparison `true` ya `false` deta hai, isliye function use seedha return kar sakta hai.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: JavaScript stops with a `SyntaxError`. Which line is wrong?
cards.code:
const add = a, b => a + b;
console.log(add(2, 3));

bug.fix: With two parameters, wrap them in brackets: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: JavaScript `SyntaxError` dekar ruk jaata hai. Kaunsi line galat hai?
hi.fix: Do parameters hon toh unhe brackets mein rakho: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`.

exercise.prompt: Fix the arrow function `isEven` so it returns `true` when n is even and `false` otherwise. The code below prints `even` or `odd` based on it.
exercise.promptHi: Arrow function `isEven` theek karo taaki n even ho toh `true` aur warna `false` return kare. Neeche ka code uske hisaab se `even` ya `odd` print karta hai.
